name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, the design-driver pattern: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.16.0 — a worktree review's `RED_BLOCKING` hard stop now writes its `GATE_RED` ledger line durably to the main root's gitignored `.claude/spec-runs.stopped.jsonl` at the moment of the stop instead of the worktree's own ledger, closing R3(1) deferred at spec 07's review: an abandoned or force-removed worktree could destroy the only record of a stopped attempt, since the row previously reached the main root only if a merge later landed. `spec-review-driver.js`'s hard-stop path self-provisions the ignore entry via git's `info/exclude` when the host lacks it (idempotent, worktree-shared — executed spike A5), and falls back loudly to today's worktree-local append when a host `.gitignore` negation pattern outranks `info/exclude` in git's precedence, naming the `.gitignore` remedy line in the STOPPED step text; the driver always names the absolute path the row landed in. `lib/observation.js`'s `readLedgerRows()` needed zero changes — it already union-merges `spec-runs*.jsonl` by filename order (executed spikes A1/A4) — so `spec-status`, `replay --due`, and `/spec:escape` see stopped rows with no reader edits. The rows drain back into the tracked ledger, positioned before the run's close row, when that spec later closes CLEAN — in-place or via merge promotion — through one spec-scoped helper called from both `promoteEvidenceAndClean()` and `doCloseWork()`. Deliberately NOT built: locking around the drain's read-modify-write window (accepted as the same order-of-magnitude race as every other multi-session ledger append this repo already lives with); extending the durable write to the CLOSE row; and a ledger row for ESCALATE, a pre-existing gap that writes no row today and stays explicitly out of scope. 7.15.1 — /spec:doctor's cited-reference check now extracts BARE FILENAMES, not just directory-prefixed paths. A path-shaped regex silently passes every directory-less citation, which is how `.claude/agents/doctrine-author.md` kept instructing every doctrine worker to add a row to `scaffold-ledger.md` — a file deleted in v7's `61e2e5a` delete-layer commit, whose function (dated justification, earned-under, mandatory retire condition) was absorbed and strengthened by core § Incident Policy's five-field bar. The stale rule is repointed at that bar; `.claude/rules/conventions/doctrine.md` had already carried the v7 wording, so the agent file was the twin the same commit did not sweep. Recorded at recurrence count one and deliberately NOT mechanized into a new sweep script: the miss was caught by eye in the same run, and core § Incident Policy earns a standing guard at a third recurrence, not a first. 7.15.0 — a due reviewer replay is now EXECUTED by review's own close instead of printed as a reminder. `spec-review-driver.js` gains a REPLAY state between MERGE's conclusion and DONE: it runs `replay.js --due` and `--select` itself, and on a due window with a selectable target it refuses to conclude the review until a `stage:"replay"` ledger row exists for that target's `reviewRunId` — joined on the run id, never a bare row count, so a concurrent session's measurement cannot satisfy this review's mark. Any recorded outcome concludes it (a non-measurement outcome leaves the harness due, so the next review retries rather than this one), and REPLAY never re-derives, re-opens, or gates the verdict — CLOSE is committed and MERGE has concluded before it runs. Motivation is measured, not argued: the advisory form shipped 2026-08-19, printed `reviewer replay due` on every CLEAN report, and was skipped through 12+ reviews in ~48 hours in this repo alone — so the driver's own copy of that reminder is retired outright rather than made louder. Two mechanical consequences ride along: the `<spec>.review/` sidecar is now deleted at DONE rather than at MERGE (REPLAY reads it), and a worktree merge relocates its state file into the main root before `merge-back cleanup` runs, since REPLAY executes after the worktree is gone. `/spec:replay` remains the manual and retry surface; its phases live in `replay.md` alone and are invoked, never restated. Landed in the same version (JJ ruling, after a Fable 5 consult on this build's own recorded debts): agent memory becomes a disposed artifact rather than a silent one. core § Feedback Loop already claimed the pipeline improves "through artifacts — never through anyone's memory" while `.claude/agent-memory/` sat outside its carrier list — written by dispatched workers, steering the next worker before any gate can observe the effect, outliving its session, derived by nothing and reviewed by nothing. Review's close now disposes every memory file a spec's diff touched, one stated fate each (carry / correct / delete), judged on what it teaches. The trigger was this build shipping a false one: two memories from a single incident both attributed the orchestrator's own concurrent edits to a phantom sibling worker and both concluded the assignment could be stood down from — one was deleted at the time, its twin rode the same commit unexamined. Deliberately NOT built, and recorded as unearned under core § Incident Policy at a recurrence count of one: any memory-review gate, write hook, or lint over the directory.
